subject: Request: Short-term credit boost for overnight latency/throughput probe
messages:
From: Elaine Park <elaine@finlytics.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 10 Nov 2025 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Short window credit request for overnight throughput/latency probe

Hi Rachel,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the model latency looked promising. We have a scheduled overnight throughput/latency probe next week and would like to request a short-term credit uplift so our infra team can validate p95/p99 with sustained load. High-level ask: 48 hours of additional trial credits starting Nov 13 (00:00 UTC) to cover an estimated ~60k–100k tokens/hr with a burst up to 150k tokens/hr during a 2-hour soak.

Attached is the POC scope (FinLytics_POC_scope.pdf) and a quick worksheet with the test plan. Can you confirm whether Redwood can provision a temporary sandbox credit top-up (no permanent pricing changes) and whether we need any contractual addendum for a one-time surge? If you need me to sign anything, happy to accelerate.

Quick context:
- Account: FinLytics (pilot)
- Objective: validate end-to-end latency at 50k+ tokens/hr sustained for 48 hours
- Start window: ideally midnight UTC on Nov 13, flexible by a few hours

Let me know next steps and who from your side we should loop in.

Thanks,
Elaine Park
Head of Platform
FinLytics
elaine@finlytics.com

Attachment: FinLytics_POC_scope.pdf (4 pages)
From: Rachel Kim <rachel@redwood.ai>
To: Elaine Park <elaine@finlytics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 10 Nov 2025 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Short window credit request for overnight throughput/latency probe

Hi Elaine — thanks for the scope and ping.

We can support a short-term credit uplift for a POC soak; I want to confirm a couple of operational details before Ben and CS scope the exact amount:
- Is the token estimate conservative or peak? You listed 60k–100k tokens/hr; is your planned steady-state ~75k tokens/hr with two planned 2-hour spikes to 150k?
- Which model variant do you expect to use (Redwood-c4 / redwood-guest quant)? If you can run on a smaller variant for the probe that helps with approvals.
- Do you need tracing/webhook telemetry to be enabled (we can hook to your S3/Datadog)?

Looping in Ben for credit approval, Soojin for runbook/CS support during the window, and Karthik to confirm compatible model variants and batching settings. Ben — if we can provision a short 48–72h sandbox uplift under deal DEAL-2025-1894, that should do it; Elaine, if you can confirm the steady-state and final start time we’ll lock it in.

Best,
Rachel Kim
Sr. Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
rachel@redwood.ai

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Elaine Park <elaine@finlytics.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 11 Nov 2025 11:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Short window credit request for overnight throughput/latency probe — provisional uplift

Hi Elaine — Ben here. Appreciate the clear scope. I've reviewed with finance and infra; we can provision a provisional credit uplift for a limited window under the pilot program. Proposed terms (provisional):

- Uplift amount: 250k tokens/day over your baseline for up to 72 hours (we recommend 72h to give you buffer).
- Start window: we can enable credits at 00:00 UTC Nov 13 per your request; confirm timezone and exact start minute.
- Operational guardrails: telemetry must be enabled during the run and we ask that you use the redwood-c4-small variant where possible to keep consistent perf numbers.
- Contractual: for one-time surges we require a short one-off addendum (DocuSign). I’ve attached SLA-exception-request.docx with the minimal terms — sign and return and we’ll finalize provisioning.

If you prefer a shorter 48h window we can reduce to 200k tokens/day. Let us know and we’ll field the DocuSign link.

Soojin — can CS standby for the run and create a short runbook? Karthik — any concerns about suggesting redwood-c4-small for the soak?

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.ai

Attachment: SLA-exception-request.docx (2 pages)
From: Elaine Park <elaine@finlytics.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 11 Nov 2025 14:46:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Short window credit request for overnight throughput/latency probe — provisional uplift

Thanks Ben — that sounds workable. We’d prefer the 48h option at 200k tokens/day, with a hard stop at the end of the window. Start: 2025-11-13 00:00 UTC (we can confirm exact minute at T-12h). We’ll enable telemetry to your S3 bucket and send the credential details to Soojin.

One question: can we use a slightly higher-capacity variant for the 2-hour soak (to reproduce peak latency) or should we stick with redwood-c4-small for the entire run? If a temporary model switch is allowed for 2 hours that would help validate tail latency at higher throughput — we can note the change in the runbook.

Attached a simple latency test plan (latency-test-plan.xlsx) with the steady-state/peak schedule. I’ll sign the addendum once I see the DocuSign link.

—Elaine
Elaine Park
Head of Platform, FinLytics

Attachment: latency-test-plan.xlsx (1 sheet)

Elaine — thanks for the quick turn. Confirming next steps and what we’ve provisioned:

- Provisioned uplift: 200k tokens/day over baseline for 48 hours (total window: 2025-11-13 00:00 UTC through 2025-11-15 00:00 UTC).
- Telemetry: please send S3 ingestion credentials to soojin@redwood.ai; CS will enable the telemetry hook and verify traces are arriving by T-6h.
- Model variant: you can run the steady-state on redwood-c4-small; we will allow a 2-hour temporary switch to redwood-c4-medium for the soak window as long as CS is onboarded and we pre-notify infra at T-12h.
- Contract: DocuSign addendum link is live here: https://app.redwood.ai/docs/docusign/addendum/DEAL-2025-1894 — please sign by EOD Nov 12 to avoid delays.
- Contact & support: Soojin will be on call (soojin@redwood.ai) during the window; Karthik will be available for config/batching advice.

We’ve queued the credit uplift and it will become active once the signed addendum is returned; if we don’t receive a signed DocuSign by 23:59 UTC Nov 12 we’ll still provision but with a short manual hold until signatures are complete (we’ll notify you).

Quick runbook below (high level):
1) T-24h: confirm start minute and telemetry credentials.
2) T-6h: CS verifies traces and runs a small warmup.
3) T-0: enable traffic ramp to steady-state.
4) Soak: run 48h, with 2h planned spike window at hour 24.
5) T+48h: run wind-down and confirm logs/telemetry export.

If anything changes, ping me directly. Looking forward to the data.

Best,
Rachel Kim
Sr. Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
rachel@redwood.ai
